I joined NPR to discuss the latest on the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran, the narrowing path to peace, and the potential for further escalations in a war that has devastated the region and created a global energy crisis. 

wbur.org/hereandnow/2026/05/…

Talked to Aljazeera about Pres Trump’s new naval mission, how it will be a resumption of conflict and a step away from the diplomatic process. This war can only end with an agreement not force.

Video

Told Aljazeera that Trump’s ego may be the biggest obstacle to deal now. 

There are signs of movement towards a deal, but President Trump’s ego may be the biggest obstacle, according to Negar Mortazavi, the host of the Iran Podcast and a senior fellow at the Center for International Policy.

“The Iranians are showing flexibility by amending and resubmitting their proposal,” she told Al Jazeera. “And I think Trump also wants to exit the war. The problem is, it has turned into an ego situation. H

I told Aljazeera Arabic that Iran did not pose a threat to the U.S. as senior U.S. officials have affirmed, and its nuclear program remains civilian.

The U.S. and Israel attacked Iran in two illegal wars of aggression, without a vote from the U.S. Congress, no vote from the UN Security Council, and despite repeated warnings from U.S. allies across the region.

Video

Pour Negar Mortazavi, du groupe de réflexion Center for International Policy, « le pouvoir iranien est assez uni et cohérent en ce moment ». Ses membres « défendent le pays, leur souveraineté, c’est une bataille existentielle », a-t-elle dit à l’AFP.
lapresse.ca/international/mo…

Analyst Negar Mortazavi, a Center for International Policy senior fellow, argued that Iran's proposal looks 'reasonable' given that the Strait of Hormuz situation has created 'a global crisis and countries around the world want it resolved.' She noted that 'Tehran will not move if the US doesn't lift its blockade, and Washington will not do so if Iran does not open the strait,' describing the offer as a potential 'first step towards a more permanent ceasefire.'
ibtimes.co.uk/trump-rejects-…

Spoke to Aljazeera about the latest message from Iran’s new supreme leader, message to the GCC and other neighbors, potentials for negotiations, and the future of the war.

Video

US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth told Congress that the “unfortunate” strike that hit an Iranian elementary school remains under investigation.

The elementary school in Minab was attacked by the IS on the first hours of the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran, killing 170 people, mostly children.

Told @AJEnglish that Iran has been under maximum pressure from the U.S. for years which hurt the people but did not produce policy change. This war will have no absolute winners or losers. Diplomacy requires flexibility and compromise from both sides.

Video

Told Aljazeera that Iran has already been under a silent economic war from the US for many years, which has severely hurt the Iranian people but produced no policy change from the government. So more economic pressure is unlikely to bring surrender.

The way out of this war is a diplomatic resolution which requires concessions from both sides so they can meet somewhere half way.

Video

Told Aljazeera that Iran’s proposal looks reasonable as the situation in the Strait of Hormuz has created a “a global crisis and countries around the world want it resolved”.

“Both Tehran and Washington need to immediately focus on reforming the Strait,” Mortazavi added. “Tehran will not move if the US doesn’t lifts its blockade, and Washington will not do so if Iran does not open the strait. Spoke to @AJEnglish about Iran’s latest proposal to the U.S. to end the war, reopen the Strait of Hormuz, and postpone nuclear talks until later.

In Doha with @Benguennak on Aljazeera, discussing the US-Israeli war on Iran and Lebanon, and the narrow path to peace between Tehran and Washington, via Islamabad, Muscat, and Moscow.

Why did this war start?

Our conversation with @AndrwPMiller, @AbuJamajem, @dylanotes.
